metadata.title: Best CHINATOWN Thai Chinese Food Walk, Bangkok | Pork Leg Stew + Shrimp Dumplings + Satay +Pennywort
metadata.description:
We embarked on Bangkok Chinatown food tour with A Chef's Tour, guided by the genial and passionate Johnny. This exhilarating experience has been split into two episodes, with today's episode covering some iconic places in the heart of Chinatown, a vibrant area known for its bustling streets, rich history, and diverse culinary offerings.

Our journey began at Auntie Noi, where we tried Gui Chai Tod, a crusty, chewy, and savory pancake made from rice flour, tapioca starch, and chives. This dish is first steamed and then pan-fried, creating a delightful texture and flavor.

Next, we visited Kamooteesam, famous for its Ka Moo, a slow-cooked stew made from pork leg and knuckle. The dish is prepared with Chinese five spices, coriander, soy sauce, oyster sauce, and sugar, resulting in a rich and flavorful experience.

Our culinary adventure continued at Je Eng Moo Satay, where we enjoyed Gai Satay. This chicken satay is marinated in a blend of turmeric, pineapple, and coconut milk, then served with a spicy peanut sauce that perfectly complements the tender and juicy chicken. We also savored Thai Suki Yaki, a Thai-style hot pot consisting of stir-fried glass noodles with veggies, a thin broth, and fermented red bean curd sauce. This dish was a comforting and hearty addition to our tour.

At Bai Bua Bok Yak Plaeng Nam, we refreshed ourselves with Nam Bai Bua Bok, a mildly sweet and earthy-flavored pennywort leaf juice. This unique drink provided a perfect balance to the savory dishes we had been enjoying.

We then made our way to Jok One Table, an eatery that, as the name suggests, has just one proper table to host a big group, requiring advance booking. Here, we relished Giaw Goong, soft and succulent dumplings stuffed with a lightly seasoned shrimp and pork mixture. The delicate flavors and textures made this dish a standout.

Our final stop was at Jek Pui Curry, a place that has even been featured in a Netflix series. We tried Gang Keaw Wan Gai/Kun Cheing, a dish consisting of rice served with a winter melon-based Thai green chicken curry and crispy, sweet pork sausage slices. The combination of the rich curry and the sweet, crispy sausage was an unforgettable ending to our tour.

Johnny's enthusiasm and knowledge made our exploration of Bangkok's Chinatown an unforgettable experience. Each eatery and dish showcased the rich culinary traditions and innovative spirit of Thai cuisine, making this tour a true feast for the senses.
